posts.title: Global by Design + Stories 'Not a studio… a Lab'
posts.copy:
Not a studio. A lab.

A studio executes the idea you already have. A lab goes looking for the one nobody has tried yet. That's how we work: AI mirrors, arcade-style games, sensor-driven installations, things people walk up to and actually touch.

Home base is Los Angeles, with partners in Miami and New York. Our last AI commercial was built by a crew in Russia for a brand launching in Brazil, which is pretty normal for us.

New website is live → sensalab.io

posts.title: Not all interactive experiences share the same goal
posts.copy:
Before picking the tech, pick the job.

The Simulator lets people try the product before they buy it.
The Collector trades a fun moment for real lead data.
The Advocate turns guests into the ones posting about your brand.

Same screen, same sensors, totally different build depending on the KPI. Which one is your next event?

posts.title: LinkedIn de Jon: lo que aprendí haciendo activaciones
posts.copy:
I've built interactive activations for brands for years. The thing nobody puts in the proposal: the tech is never what fails. It's the queue, the Wi-Fi, the staff who weren't trained, the screen nobody could see from the aisle.

That's why every Sensa Lab build gets tested in our own space before it ships.

What's the most unexpected thing that broke at one of your events?

posts.title: Top AI experiential booths
posts.copy:
Three AI booths we keep coming back to:

Intel at CES made data processing something you could see happen in front of you.
Salesforce at Dreamforce turned attendee data into AI trading cards people actually kept.
Vonage told its cloud story through an interactive hero you got to play.

The common thread: none of them explained the product. They let you use it. Swipe for the breakdown.

posts.title: Perception vs. Reality
posts.copy:
What people think: interactive tech is fragile and something will crash in front of the client.

What actually happens when it's built right: it runs all day, the queue keeps growing and nobody thinks about the tech at all.

Most of our work is the boring part nobody sees. Testing, backups, a plan B for the Wi-Fi.

posts.title: Signature Experience: Sensa Mirror
posts.copy:
Sensa Mirror.

Guests step in front of it, AI restyles them in your brand's world, and they walk away with a photo they actually want to post. Every shot carries your logo and every share is opt-in lead data.

Ready in three weeks. Ask us for the deck.

posts.title: What is white label?
posts.copy:
For agencies: you sell the experience, we build it.

We work white label with experiential agencies across the US. Development, real-time logic, hardware and on-site tech, all under your brand. Your client never has to know we exist (unless you want to brag about us).

DMs are open.

posts.title: Road to LA 2028 #1: 10x activaciones
posts.copy:
Summer 2028 is coming to LA, and the people running the sponsor program expect roughly ten times as many brand activations as at Milano Cortina.

That means agencies are already scoping, and the good tech partners will be booked early. We're LA-based and building for it now.

Agencies: if you're scoping 2028, let's talk early.

posts.title: Why traditional marketing isn't working anymore
posts.copy:
Walk any expo floor and count the booths with a banner, a looping video and someone handing out pens.

Now count the ones with a line.

People don't remember what a brand told them. They remember what they did there. That's the whole case for experiential.

posts.title: The brands you remember don't just advertise
posts.copy:
Nike x SNIPES in Brooklyn: a photo booth that turned every visitor into a content creator.
Adidas 'Faster Than': treadmills in-store, real-time metrics, the product proving itself.
Adidas in Dubai: a billboard you could literally swim in.

None of these were about budget. They were about giving people something to do. Which one would you have stood in line for?

posts.title: Is your activation just for decoration?
posts.copy:
If it looks great in photos but nobody touches it, it's decoration.

An activation should do a job: capture leads, explain the product, get people posting. If you can't name the job, the build isn't done yet.

posts.title: Signature Experience: Sensa Playboard
posts.copy:
Sensa Playboard turns your product catalog into a game on a table.

Tap, match, win. People learn your lineup without reading a single spec sheet, and you get to see which products they played with most.

posts.title: The most visited booth is the most interactive
posts.copy:
The most visited booth at any expo isn't the biggest. It's the most interactive.

How that plays out by industry:
Tech, gaming and automotive: motion tracking where your body controls the screen.
Fashion and beauty: an AI avatar that puts the visitor inside the brand.
B2B: live data where every interaction feeds a leaderboard.

Which one fits your next show?
